description: We are TED Eskişehir Koleji students united by our passion for space science and data exploration. As "Turkish Space Lines," we combine programming, design, and storytelling to make NASA data accessible to younger audiences. We seek collaborators skilled in web development (HTML/CSS) and game design (JavaScript/Unity) to build our interactive platform. Together, we will transform scientific data into a fun, educational journey.
summary: Space Salvage Squad is an interactive and story-driven space exploration game designed to transform complex archival data of past NASA missions into an engaging learning experience. While space missions eventually end, the data they collect continues to shape science. However, accessing this information is often difficult for younger audiences. Our project bridges this gap by turning the stories of abandoned or completed missions (such as Apollo, Opportunity, InSight, and Voyager) into an exploratory adventure where players learn through mission maps, storytelling, and problem-solving scenarios.
details:
What it does & How it addresses the challenge: Space Salvage Squad addresses the "Abandoned But Not Forgotten: Storytelling About NASA's Leftover Equipment on the Moon and Mars" challenge by gamifying historical space assets. Players navigate a destination map covering the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space, exploring missions like Apollo laser reflectors, the Opportunity and InSight rovers, and Voyager. Players learn mission histories, evaluate challenges, and select appropriate engineering solutions to gain feedback and score.

Benefits & Impact:

  • Scientific Awareness: Teaches the purpose and discoveries of historical space vehicles.
  • Critical Thinking: Encourages players to evaluate problems and make informed decisions.
  • STEM Skills: Sparks curiosity in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics among school-aged students and youth.

Tools, Languages & Technologies:

  • Built with web/game development tools focusing on interactive maps, UI/UX design, and gamification elements (leaderboards, progress tracking).
  • Content structured using official NASA mission archives and data.
